sources.note: Nothing. Atong appears in Table 5 (p.11: ISO ATO, other name Etoh, 4,200 speakers, 5 villages), Table 6 (p.12, 'Bibliographic resources for Western Momo languages': Atong -> Ayotte & Ayotte (2002) only) and as a tone-marked column of the comparative Western Momo wordlist (Table 7, pp.13-17; tone key p.iv: High acute, Mid unmarked, Low grave, Rising, Falling). Sec. 1.2 notes 'SIL survey wordlists are always recorded phonetically'. No stress/accent statement (0 hits).

sources.citation: Ayotte, Michael & Charlene Ayotte. 2002. Rapid appraisal and lexicostatistical analysis surveys of Atong, Ambele, and Menka (Widikum-Menka Subdivision, Momo Division, North West Province). SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2002-076. 43 pp. (Glottolog ref 133897)
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic rapid-appraisal survey: sec. 5.2 'Atong' (villages Akanunku, Anjing, Atong, Ekao, Emuah; autonym Etoh; 'Speakers of Atong report no variation within the language'; multilingualism, vitality, attitudes); sec. 2.2: 126-item ALCAM wordlists, not tape-recorded; Appendix F: Atong wordlists (Akanunku, Emuah) in a legacy SIL phonetic font, diacritics garbled in the text layer. No phonology section; grep stress/accent/prosod/tone = 0 hits.
